newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish T-bill yields seen inching down at tender.
newsitem.headline: Polish T-bill yields seen inching down at tender.

text.p: Polish T-bill yields are expected to inch down at the Monday 650 million zloty primary auction under large demand, analysts said on Friday.
They said domestic investors would bid for between 1.2 and 1.3 billion zlotys worth of the bills but said foreign investors would likely again remain on the sidelines.
"Yields are likely to inch down at next week's tender as banks and clients are looking for investment paper," said Bartlomiej Kumela, senior T-bill dealer at Societe Generale.

Analysts said the average yields of the 13-week and 26-week T-bill would likely decline by between 0.05 to 0.10 point from 18.60 and 19.11 percent respectively on September 16, the last time the treasury offered bills of this length.

"The 13- and 26-week paper is attactive for non-bank clients and there seems to be a lot of competition between banks to service such clients," said Wojciech Kowalczyk, T-bill dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
Analysts said the average yield of the benchmark 52-week T-bill would likely stay in the region of 19.44 percent.
In secondary trade on Friday one-year T-bills were traded around 19.40 percent and half-year paper around 19.15 percent.
On Monday the treasury will offer 100 million zlotys worth of 13-week T-bills, 200 million zlotys worth of 26-week bills and 350 million zlotys of the benchmark paper.
Analysts said the end-of-the-month cash shortage on the money market, which drove one-day rates above the 25 percent lombard rate should end next week as a new reserve period begins on Monday.
They said one-day rates would gradually return to the main 14-day drainage rate of 19.13 percent as NBP-bill redemption and reverse-repo buy-back inflows increased liquidity.

The zloty was seen holding basically stable against the basket of currencies next week, using dollar/mark fluctuations as guideposts for moves in the absence of large client orders to spark trends, analysts said.
They said the zloty should continue to reign within its weeks-long range between 1.9 and 1.5 percent below the centre of its 14-percent daily trading band, called the parity rate.
"If the situation on the money market returns to the norm as expected, I see the zloty to trade stable to lower next week," said Przemyslaw Ciszecki of ING bank in Warsaw.
The zloty closed the week at 2.8010 to the dollar and at 1.8380 per mark, or about 1.90 percent from the parity rate.
